baseline.name: Reverse one construction step at a time
baseline.approach: Use the current maximum and subtract the sum of other entries once per reverse step, restoring the heap each time.
baseline.time: O(n+s log n), for s individual reverse steps

archived.name: Modulo-batched reverse max-heap
archived.time: O(n+r log n), for r modulo-reduction iterations
archived.space: O(n) heap and O(log n) recursive heapify stack

why: When the other entries stay fixed, a remainder operation compresses repeated subtractions of their sum; rest==1 is resolved immediately.
quantitative_comparison: Replacing x by x%rest can skip many individual x-=rest reverse steps before another element becomes maximal. The number skipped depends on the current values; no fixed improvement factor or measured runtime ratio is asserted.
tradeoffs: Benefits depend on the target values. The source assumes positive nonempty input, bounded long long sums and successful heap allocation; arithmetic shortcuts do not replace those preconditions.
evidence_basis: Static reverse-state arithmetic and heap loop comparison; no empirical benchmark.
